deathSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Moshe Simon. Community gardener. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Lucky Coin, Knife roll, Home key, Beat-up Paperback, Dead Phone. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.

"Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Valeria asks "Tell me you didn't go alone." Sofia says "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
